The WW2 generation crossed oceans without apps and rebuilt a nation without consulting fees. Eighty years later, Canada spent over half a trillion dollars on a pandemic response — and cannot account for where much of it went. The Auditor General's reports, the Parliamentary Budget Officer's trackers, and Parliamentary committee testimony document a pattern of spending without oversight,…

The PBO's COVID-19 Cost Tracker documented over $500 billion in federal spending measures announced between March 2020 and the wind-down of pandemic programs. This figure encompasses direct transfers to individuals, business subsidies, health procurement, provincial transfers, and the alphabet soup of emergency programs — CERB, CEWS, CEBA, CECRA, CERS, CRB, CRCB, CRSB — that defined the federal…

The Department of Finance's Fiscal Monitor and the PBO's Fiscal Sustainability Report document the consequence: federal debt surged from approximately $721 billion before the pandemic to over $1.06 trillion by the end of fiscal year 2021–22 — an increase of roughly $348 billion in two years. To put that in generational terms, it took Canada from Confederation in 1867 to the year 2020 — 153 years…
